title: Make Review Verification Requests Executable Without Reviewer-Supplied Literal Commands
specification:
# PRD: Make Review Verification Requests Executable Without Reviewer-Supplied Literal Commands

Priority: high

## Problem
Implementation follow-ups only treat reviewer verification requests as actionable when the review text includes a literal runnable command. Requests phrased as focused verification, named test files, or affected areas do not reliably become executable required checks, so agents can loop or noop instead of running the appropriate test themselves.

## Goal
Allow implementation follow-ups to derive, run, and record the correct verification command from reviewer intent when the reviewer specifies files, suites, or risk areas rather than an exact shell command.

## Requirements
- Extend review blocker extraction so file-based or suite-based verification requests are normalized into structured executable verification targets, not just freeform notes.
- Define a deterministic resolver that maps changed files and reviewer-mentioned test files/areas to one or more runnable commands.
- Require implementation follow-ups to execute or explicitly fail the resolved verification command before completion when an open verification blocker exists.
- Record the chosen command, pass/fail result, and evidence on the follow-up task so reviewer gating uses structured proof.
- Prevent noop completion and reviewer approval when a verification blocker remains unresolved because no command was resolved or executed.
- Add fallback behavior for ambiguous requests: mark the blocker unresolved with a clear reason instead of silently accepting noop completion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A review request that references a test file or focused area without a literal shell command produces a follow-up task with at least one concrete executable verification command.
- An implementation follow-up with an open verification blocker cannot complete until the resolved command is run and recorded as passing, or the task remains blocked with a clear unresolved reason.
- Reviewer approval and auto-approval paths refuse to approve while derived verification blockers remain unresolved.
- Task/state history shows which reviewer request produced which resolved command and which follow-up run satisfied it.

## Verification
- Unit tests for blocker extraction from review text that mentions files or focused verification without explicit commands.
- Unit tests for command resolution from changed files and mentioned test targets.
- Unit tests proving noop completion is blocked when a verification blocker has no passing recorded result.
- Smoke test covering review request -> follow-up resolves command -> command runs -> reviewer approval.

tasks.title: Normalize reviewer verification requests into executable verification targets
tasks.description: Extend the review blocker extraction and follow-up creation flow so reviewer requests phrased as test files, suites, focused verification areas, or affected-risk guidance are converted into structured verification blocker records with deterministic executable command candidates rather than remaining prose-only notes. Implement a resolver that uses reviewer-mentioned targets together with changed files and existing project test conventions to derive one or more runnable commands, and preserve the originating reviewer request on the blocker so downstream logic can trace the command back to the review. Likely touch points include reviewer feedback parsing, follow-up task creation, queue/spec serialization, and command-resolution helpers under `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, `src/sync/`, and any shared task or review-state contract modules that shape follow-up requirements.
acceptance: A review request that names a test file, test suite, or focused verification area without supplying a literal shell command creates a structured verification blocker on the implementation follow-up task with at least one concrete runnable command when the request is resolvable from repository context.

The structured blocker records the originating reviewer request, the resolved command or commands, the resolution basis such as mentioned file, suite, or changed-file match, and a blocker status that distinguishes resolved commands from unresolved ambiguity.
Command resolution is deterministic for the same review request and changed-file context and does not depend on agent freeform judgment once inputs are fixed.

When reviewer wording is too ambiguous to resolve into a command, the follow-up task records the blocker as unresolved with a clear machine-readable reason instead of treating the request as satisfied or dropping it into prose-only notes.
Structured verification blocker data survives task persistence and reload paths so later implementation and reviewer steps can consume the same reviewer-request-to-command mapping.

Unit coverage is added for blocker extraction from review text that references files or focused verification areas without explicit commands, plus unit coverage for deterministic command resolution from changed files and mentioned test targets.

tasks.title: Require execution evidence for verification blockers before follow-up completion or approval
tasks.description: Update implementation follow-up execution, completion gating, and reviewer approval logic so open structured verification blockers must either run a resolved command and record passing evidence or remain blocked with an explicit unresolved or failed reason. Persist the chosen command, execution result, and proof onto the follow-up task or related tracked state, and ensure reviewer approval and auto-approval paths refuse approval while a derived verification blocker lacks a passing recorded result. Likely touch points include follow-up runner behavior, completion state transitions, reviewer gating, PR/history or queue-state evidence recording, and reconstruction logic under `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, `src/sync/`, and any reviewer/runtime state modules that evaluate blocker satisfaction.
acceptance: An implementation follow-up with an open verification blocker cannot complete as success, done, merged, or `noop` until a resolved verification command has been executed and recorded as passing, or the blocker remains open with a clear unresolved or failed reason.
If no command can be resolved for a verification blocker, completion logic leaves the blocker unresolved with explicit reasoning and does not silently allow noop completion.
Follow-up task or tracked state data records, for each verification blocker, the chosen command, execution status, evidence of the run, and which follow-up attempt satisfied or failed it.
Reviewer approval and any reviewer auto-approval path refuse to approve while a derived verification blocker remains unresolved, unexecuted, or lacks a passing recorded result.

Task or state history exposes which reviewer request produced which resolved command and which follow-up execution satisfied it so reviewer gating relies on structured proof rather than summary prose.

Unit tests prove noop or equivalent successful completion is blocked when a verification blocker has no passing recorded result, and smoke coverage exercises the review request to follow-up resolution to command execution to reviewer approval path.
Verification for the implementation includes `npm run typecheck` and the relevant focused unit and smoke tests covering review follow-up enforcement and approval gating.
